title: Philippine Red Cross activated its typhoon Early Action Protocol on 510's machine-learning impact forecast before Storm Nalgae (October 2022)
summary: A machine-learning damage forecast from 510 met the early-action trigger on 27 October 2022, and the Philippine Red Cross installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae.
account: The Philippine Red Cross approved its Early Action Protocol for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting model, developed with 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross, applies machine learning to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. In 2021 the 510 model also became the trigger model for the anticipatory action pilot of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the Philippines. The Central Emergency Response Fund funded the OCHA pilot with $7.5 million for the 2023 typhoon season. Under the protocol, early actions start when the forecast shows at least 10 percent of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510 forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That met the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. The final report says that the 56-hour lead time was exceptionally granted. With anticipatory funds from the Disaster Response Emergency Fund of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the Philippine Red Cross activated the protocol in Aurora Province. From 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. The final report says that strong winds and the onset of rain limited the distribution to 78 households. The Philippine Red Cross's post-storm survey reports that all 78 kits were installed and that 390 people were reached. The operation spent CHF 7,002 of its CHF 117,555 budget. The final report of 30 June 2023 records that a lessons-learned workshop judged the trigger high and recommended a review of the protocol. The Philippine Red Cross renewed its typhoon protocol and first activated the renewed protocol in November 2025, when it installed shelter strengthening kits in Quirino, Isabela and Quezon-Lucena. The annual report on that activation does not name the trigger model.

ai_role.statement: The ML impact forecast was the trigger. Under the EAP, early actions fire on the forecast wind impact on housing 72 hours before landfall. The trigger: at least 10% of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities. The notification records the Aurora municipalities as “Met (More than 10%)”. fields.summary: A machine-learning damage forecast from 510 met the early-action trigger on 27 October 2022, and the Philippine Red Cross installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae.
fields.account: The Philippine Red Cross approved its Early Action Protocol for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting model, developed with 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross, applies machine learning to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. In 2021 the 510 model also became the trigger model for the anticipatory action pilot of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the Philippines. The Central Emergency Response Fund funded the OCHA pilot with $7.5 million for the 2023 typhoon season. Under the protocol, early actions start when the forecast shows at least 10 percent of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510 forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That met the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. The final report says that the 56-hour lead time was exceptionally granted. With anticipatory funds from the Disaster Response Emergency Fund of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the Philippine Red Cross activated the protocol in Aurora Province. From 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. The final report says that strong winds and the onset of rain limited the distribution to 78 households. The Philippine Red Cross's post-storm survey reports that all 78 kits were installed and that 390 people were reached. The operation spent CHF 7,002 of its CHF 117,555 budget. The final report of 30 June 2023 records that a lessons-learned workshop judged the trigger high and recommended a review of the protocol. The Philippine Red Cross renewed its typhoon protocol and first activated the renewed protocol in November 2025, when it installed shelter strengthening kits in Quirino, Isabela and Quezon-Lucena. The annual report on that activation does not name the trigger model.
